## What landed

**(1) G4-1 — the oauth timing flake: a real fencepost defect, repaired.**
`hh-mcp-lab/tests/r2_19.rs::credential_mediator_oauth_resolves_and_refuses`
mints a zero-TTL caller token (`mint_caller_token("mcp://lab", 0)`) and
asserts `resolve_credential` answers `CredentialExpired`.
`CredentialBroker::mint` sets `expires_at_ms = now + ttl`; the old
`verify_minted` compared `now_ms > expires_at_ms` — so a verify landing
in the *same millisecond* as the zero-TTL mint returned `Valid` instead
of `Expired`, and the assertion panicked only when mint→resolve stayed
inside one ms window. Six recorded CI firings (R2.22 `dc7061d`, R2.23
`cb6db76`, R2.25 `d8fd2e4`, R2.26 `e377a4a` + `9ad4e60`) — rising
cadence, exactly the defect class the ticket named. Fix:
`crates/hh-secrets/src/broker.rs` `>` → `>=` (the `now < exp` reading —
RFC 7519; the crate's own `CallerBinding::live_at` and `mediate`
`expires_at <= ts_now` conventions already agreed). A zero-TTL mint is
born expired. New regression test
`hh-secrets/tests/r2_10.rs::r2_10_minted_token_expires_at_the_expiry_instant`
pins both sides (`expires_at_ms - 1` → Valid; `expires_at_ms` →
Expired; zero-TTL → Expired at mint). **25/25 in-process runs green.**

**(2) G4-2 — the `ac5` `derived_from.view_hash` parity member:
adjudicated to the allowlist, derivation input named.** Root cause:
`context.assembled` is an observation-plane row, so a *later*
assembly's `derived_from.view_hash` is the `idp/1` stamp of the
`context_view` fold over the durable prefix — which includes the
earlier rows' measured `assembly_ms.value` wall (already allowlisted
at R2.1). A millisecond crossing in one leg diverges the downstream
view_hash mechanically — a derived consequence, not an independent
input. The alternative (excluding measured walls from the projection)
would weaken the AC-R-2.2.1-3 rebuild contract, so
`derived_from.view_hash` joined the existing `ends_with` convention in
`crates/hh-cli/tests/in_process.rs` with the derivation input named in
the comment (CC1 — one allowlist convention). **25/25 runs green
post-change (65 total across the session).** LEDGER finding
repaired-closed with evidence.

**(3) G4-7 — the `r2_14` loopback `Connection reset`: a fixture defect,
repaired.** `LocalHttpTransport::forward` writes head and body in two
`write_all` calls; both loopback sinks (`hh-embed/tests/r2_14.rs`,
`hh-env/tests/egress_mediation.rs`) stopped reading at `\r\n\r\n` and
answered + dropped the socket — a split segment left the body unread at
close → RST → client `read_to_end` saw `Connection reset` (the R2.21
`52e46d4` firing). Both fixtures now consume the declared
`Content-Length` body before responding (`read_request`) —
protocol-correct HTTP, clean FIN. No retry added. **25/25 runs green.**
Bonus determinism: the sink assertions on `"event_id"` body content now
always see the body.

**(4) Bookkeeping sweep (G4-4/5/6).** DEFERRALS.md: 16 discharged cells
whose status cell led `OPEN`/`PARTIAL` flipped to `DONE` — dated
`**DONE**` evidence preserved verbatim, no landed text touched. The
17th candidate, DF-S0.3-3, keeps its `PARTIAL` lead: its marker is
scoped (`**machine cells DONE**`) and the R2 human-signature residual
is genuinely open (BL-02, HUMAN-H4). DF-S2.4-2 gains a dated
`residual note 2026-10-14 (R3.1)` naming BL-31 (`env`). BACKLOG.md
"How to read" corrected: the G4-4 wart sentence now records the R3.1
sweep and the post-sweep truth (72 DONE / 25 OPEN / 3 PARTIAL — leading
tokens and dated markers now agree). BACKLOG.csv BL-42 gained
ADR-0354 (45 standing triggers); `check-backlog.sh` exit 0.

**ADR-0354** records the three adjudications (inclusive expiry, the
